value.rationale: The Heawood graph is a canonical small, highly symmetric Pfaffian cubic brace. Minimal knowledge sufficient to specify one of its perfect matchings is a natural information-theoretic and combinatorial invariant. The seven explicit maximal competing intersections give a structural complete characterization; the two inequivalent optimal triple families and exact cardinality polynomial distinguish configurations not implied by a scalar forcing number, matching count, or Hamiltonian 2-factor property. The result is finite but fully classified and mathematically motivated, not an arbitrary slice.
